messages:
pagerduty-bot: [PagerDuty] PAGER - High: inference-queue-high-5xx (service: inference-api)
Severity: P1 | Region: eu-west-1 | Trigger: 5xx spike from model-serving -> 65% error rate over 1m.
Linked incident: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD-12345
Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/inference-high-5xx

sara.k: acked via PagerDuty (oncall-eu). I'm jumping on this — putting a quick bridge up. @li.chen if it escalates please standby.

mike.d: available if needed. tagging @priya.n for LB check. :thumbsup:

sara.k: quick triage, looking at pods in eu-west-1:
```
$ kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide | grep model-serving
model-serving-0   CrashLoopBackOff   3/3   1d   10.1.2.34
model-serving-1   5/5   Running   20h   10.1.2.35
model-serving-2   0/3   Error     2m    10.1.2.36
```
Logs show repeated KV cache OOMs and 5xx responses from the runtime: 
```
2026-03-14T15:12:02Z ERROR runtime: kv_cache_eviction failed: out of memory
2026-03-14T15:12:04Z WARN http: downstream 503 for request id=abcd1234
```
Suspect memory pressure on several GPU nodes + a hot routing pattern causing oversized KV growth.

pagerduty-bot: No update in 2m -> auto-escalating to next responder: li.chen

li.chen: taking over (oncall-sre). Kicking off scale steps and temporary routing fallback. Steps I'm running now:
- scale dedicated pool (eu inference) +4 GPUs
- enable prefix/KV cache TTL short-circuit for active sessions
- route new traffic to lighter model variant r2-8b as fallback

li.chen: running infra command:```
infractl scale --pool inference-eu --add-gpus 4 --reason "auto-escalate PD"```

li.chen: and applying rate cap on public route to reduce surge:```
rlctl set-rate --route /v1/generate --max-rps 250 --burst 500```

priya.n: networking check: saw healthcheck flapping on 10.1.2.36 and 10.1.2.34, backend connection resets. I'm draining the two hosts from the LB to stop noisy retries and will monitor.

sara.k: handoff: li.chen you're primary. I'll stay on bridge for customer comms and post a customer-impact blurb.

sara.k: CUSTOMER IMPACT (quick): approx 7% of production requests experienced 5xx in eu-west-1 over the 10m window. Latency also spiked 200-400ms on successful responses. A subset of requests to large-context models are failing because of KV blowup. No data loss; requests will be retried by clients.

li.chen: scaled pool completed, new nodes registering:
```
INFO infractl: pool inference-eu now 12 GPUs (was 8) - nodes: gpu-eu-07,gpu-eu-08,gpu-eu-09,gpu-eu-10
kubectl get pods -> model-serving replicas back to 5/5 on all nodes
```
Routing fallback to r2-8b applied via runtime config: `/models/current -> r2-8b (fallback)`

li.chen: monitoring metrics -> errors dropping: 65% -> 3% in last 90s. Latency normalizing. Will keep the rate cap until stable.

mike.d: :white_check_mark: nice work. Can you drop a short postmortem TODO in this thread with next steps for mitigating KV growth long term?

li.chen: TODOs:
- collect heap profiles from affected nodes (runtime/kv cache)
- add conservative per-session KV size guard and eviction watermark
- create automated alert for prefix-cache growth > 500MB per session
- postmortem & customer comms draft in #incidents once stable

incident-bot: Bridge created: https://meet.example/bridge/incident-1749994321 | Duration: ongoing

sara.k: TL;DR for customers: "We've identified a transient memory pressure issue in the inference runtime in eu-west-1 causing elevated 5xx errors. We've scaled capacity, applied temporary rate limiting and routed new traffic to a fallback model. Errors are falling; we continue monitoring. ETA update in 30m."

li.chen: marking incident state -> monitoring. Will let PD auto-resolve when error rate <1% for 10m, or I'll resolve manually.

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD-12345 updated: state=under_investigation -> monitoring (escalation cleared).

sara.k: thanks all — closing handoff. li.chen you're owner; I'll update PG customers if we need to widen comms. :v:

li.chen: acknowledged; staying on watch for 30m. will post final status when we hit stable window.

pagerduty-bot: If service returns to normal, this alert will auto-resolve. Current error rate: 0.8% (1m).

sara.k: closing notes: immediate mitigations = scale up GPUs, drain flaky hosts, apply rate cap, fallback model. Next: root-cause run and KV eviction hardening.

li.chen: final status ping: 15:21 UTC -> errors at 0.3%, latency back to baseline. Leaving incident in monitoring for 30m then closing. :lock_with_ink_pen:
